summary: Title Case can discard an invalid slash-containing replacement prefix before validation, resulting in a lossy valid-looking rename.

judgment.rationale: The transformation path can erase the invalid separator before validation: Title Case treats the replacement as a filesystem path and emits only its stem, then DoRename checks the shortened result. Validate the original replacement first and keep invalid status independent of transformed display text.
evidence: The live report gives a concrete invalid-name repro: replacement draft/report should be rejected, but Title Case previews Report.txt and Apply uses the shortened name.

proposed_fixes.title: Validate replacement characters before case formatting
proposed_fixes.root_cause: DoRename applies GetTransformedFileName before checking for invalid filename characters. The Title Case transform parses the replacement with std::filesystem::path and uses stem/extension, which drops the directory portion of draft/report; the subsequent invalid-character check therefore sees only Report and cannot reject the original slash.
plan: Validate the raw replacement component for forbidden filename characters before any case transform or filesystem stem/extension parsing can discard characters.
Keep the invalid-name status and preview behavior tied to the original replacement while preserving existing filename/extension scope rules for valid input.
Add regression tests for both slash directions in a Title Case replacement and confirm preview marks the item invalid and Apply skips it.
verification: Run focused PowerRename native tests for invalid replacement validation and Title Case.
Repeat foo.txt with Filename + extension, Search=foo, Replace=draft/report, Title Case; the preview must flag the invalid character and Apply must not create Report.txt.

confidence.rationale: The public repro and current source ordering align directly: path parsing removes the separator before the later validator checks it. The proposed validation-before-transform change is narrow and directly testable.
